newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BOK intervenes to cap dollar's rise vs won-dealers.
newsitem.headline: BOK intervenes to cap dollar's rise vs won-dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) stepped into the interbank forex market early Monday to halt the dollar's rise against the won, dealers said.
Dealers said the central bank began selling dollars at 824.30 won. After the intervention, the won rose to 823.60.
"Given importer deals due today and a shortage of the dollar's market position, the intervention was expected," said a local bank dealer.
Though the central bank has never confirmed an intervention in the market, dealers said there were no other reasons to explain the dollar's fall.
They said the dollar could soar to the 826.00 won level without dollar sales by the BOK.
